description: The 11300 block of Rojas Dr is a local road that travels east to west and consists of a designated left turn lane, two lanes traveling west, and two lanes traveling east. U1 crashed into U2 causing damages to the rear bumper and trunk of U2. No onsite investigation conducted. U2 was assigned a case number. Diagram is approximate.

Unit—02 was in the far right lane on 12300 Edgemere facing east stopped at a red light. Unit—01 was directly behind Unit—02 in the same lane facing east stopped at the red light. The driver of Unit—01 stated he began to roll forward to close the distance, and by unknown reason accelerated forward striking Unit—02 from the rear. Unit—02 received the listed rear damage. Unit—01 received the listed front end damage. No injuries were reported, and no independent witnesses were located. The officers issued Unit—01's driver for failure to control speed causing an accident.

3300 block of Yarbrough is four Lane two way roadway that travels north and south with a mandatory left turn lane which intersects with the 10600 block of Edgemere which is a four lane two way roadway that travels east and west with a mandatory leftturn lane. Unit 3 was at a complete stop Waiting at the lights of Edgemere and Yarbough in order to continue east on Edgemere. Driver of Unit 1 advised that he entered the intersection on a green arrow and started to make a left turn onto Edgemere. Driver of Unit 2 advised that as he was approaching and entering the intersection Unit 1 made a left turn in front of him causing him not to be able to stop on time and struck Unit 1 causing the listed damage. Driver of Unit 3 advised that as she was waiting for the lights to change to continued east, she observed Unit 1 entered the intersection in front of Unit 2 which collided with Unit 1 and Unit 1 traveled est on Edgemere and struck Unit 3. Passengers to Unit 1 were transported to Del Sol hospital for medical attention by Rescue18 and the driver of Unit 2 was transported to del sol Hospital for medical attention.

The driver of Unit 1 stated that as she was traveling eastbound on Trawood, she proceeded through the intersection at George Dieter with a solid green light, when she collided with Unit 2, who was traveling southbound on George Dieter. The driver of Unit 2 stated that as he was traveling southbound on George Dieter, he proceeded through the intersection at Trawood with a solid green light, when he collided with Unit 1. Both Unit 1 and Unit 2 stated they had solid green lights. No witnesses remained at the scene, and no injuries were reported.

Driver of Unit 1 assumed Unit 2 was making a left turn onto Edgemere Blvd., instead, Unit 2 continued northbound

There were no independent witnesses regarding the accident.

WESTBOUND AND EASTBOUND LANES ARE DIVIDED BY A RAISED MEDIAN. 3100 TRAWOOD NORTHBOUND IS A SIX LANE / TWO WAY WITH ONE MANDATORY LEFT TURN AND TWO MANDATORY RIGHT TURN LANE. 3100 TRAWOOD SOUTHBOUND IS A FIVE LANE / TWO WAY WITH A MANDATORY LEFT AND RIGHT LANE. The 12700 block of Tierra Este is a 5 lane marked roadway with 3 lanes traveling northbound and 2 lanes traveling southbound divided by a painted divider. The 12700 block of Tierra Este intersects with the 12400 block of Edgemere, a 6 lane marked roadway with 3 lanes traveling west and 3 lanes traveling east divided by a painted divider. Driver of Unit 2 stated that Unit 1 was traveling West on the 12400 block of Edgemere and ran the stop sign thus causing Unit 1 to collide into unit 2 thus causing Unit 2 to collide into Unit 3. Driver of Unit 3 stated that he was traveling South on the 12400 block of Tierra Este in the number 3 lane directly next to Unit 2 when Driver of Unit 1 collided into Unit 2 thus causing Unit 2 to collide into Unit 3. No witnesses stood by for the officers at the scene. Passenger of Unit 2 was transported by EMS to Sierra Providence east on a possible injury.

The driver of unit 1 was north on 1400 Lee Trevino when he failed to control his speed and collided with unit 2 who was directly behind unit 3 which was waiting in traffic for a green signal. Unit 2 and 3 were also north on 1400 N Lee Trevino. Unit 1 collided with unit 2 pushing it forward causing it to collide with unit 3, and causing the damage. The driver of unit 1 claimed no injuries. The driver of unit 3 claimed no injuries at the time of the incident but mentioned they had a headache and declined.medical attention. No witnesses  came forward at the scene.

10600 EDGEMERE is a 2 way east/west roadway with 2 lanes east and 2 lanes west divided by a double yellow line and controlled by a traffic light at Yarbrough. 3300 N YARBROUGH is a 2 way north/south roadway with 2 lanes north and 2 lanes south divided by a raised median and controlled by a traffic light. Officers and EMS personnel were not able to detect any alcohol on breath on the driver of unit 1. Driver ofunit 1 did stated they have been up all day and the night before taking care of a family member at the hospital.
Unit 2 was traveling NB on Lee Trevino Dr in the center lane and as at a complete stop at a red light when Unit 2 approached from behind and did not stop. Unit 2 was rear—ended by Unit 1.

The 3000 block of Lee Trevino is a six-lane (divided/unprotected) roadway for northbound and southbound travel. The 3000 block of Lee Trevino has two double mandatory left-turn-only lanes, one on the southbound lanes and one on the northbound lanes. The 10900 block of Pebble Hills is a four-lane (divided/unprotected) roadway with both westbound and eastbound travel. The 10900 block of Pebble Hills contains two mandatory left-turn-only lanes, one on the eastbound lanes and one on the westbound lanes. Unit 1 stated she was traveling southbound on the 3000 block of Lee Trevino in the far-left lane to proceed onto the 10900 block of Pebble Hills and had the green arrow when she took the turn. The driver of Unit 1 stated that this was all she could remember. The driver of Unit 2 stated he was traveling northbound on the 3000 block of Lee Trevino in the far-left lane to continue north and was going to cross the intersection of the 10900 block of Pebble Hills. The driver of Unit 2 stated he had the green light and was proceeding through when he observed Unit 1 traveling westbound in the eastbound lanes of 10900 Pebble Hills. The driver of Unit 2 stated Unit 1 crossed at an extremely high rate of speed, and he could not avoid the collision. The driver of Unit 2 stated he applied his brakes and tried to swerve out of the way but could not do so in time, causing Unit 2 to collide with Unit 1. No injuries were reported at the scene. Witness 1 stated she was traveling northbound on the 3000 block of Lee Trevino and was in the far-right lane to turn eastbound onto the 10900 block of Pebble Hills. Witness 1 stated that as she was proceeding to turn with a solid green light, she observed Unit 1 traveling westbound in the eastbound lanes of 10900 Pebble Hills. Witness 1 stated she activated her horn to alert the driver of Unit 1 that they were traveling on the wrong side of the road. Witness 1 stated that before Unit 1 entered the intersection, Unit 1 came to a stop as the signal light was red for 10900 Pebble Hills.

Unit 1 stated he was traveling South on N Lee Trevino Dr in the left lane to continue straight and Unit 2 was in the middle lane also to continue straight. Unit 1 stated that when the light turned green for all lanes except for the dedicated left turn lanes, for unknown reasons, Unit 2 cut in front of Unit 1 right before the intersection in an attempt to merge into one of the left turn only lanes. Unit 1 struck Unit 2 causing damages to Unit 2‘s rear left bumper while Unit 1 sustained damages to the front.

The 2900 block of Trawood is a 5 lane roadway that travels in the direction of East and West with two lanes traveling eastbound and two lanes traveling westbound and a mandatory turn lane.
